title: Mahindra to Double EV Capacity Over Five Years as Q1 Profit Rises 6.8%
excerpt: India's largest SUV maker plans to scale electric vehicle production amid robust demand, even as Middle East-driven commodity costs squeeze auto margins.
body:
• Mahindra & Mahindra will double its EV production capacity over the next five years, CEO Anish Shah confirmed after Q1 results.
  • Q1 consolidated net profit rose 6.8% to ₹36.85 billion ($4.3 billion in revenue), with SUV segment revenue climbing 24.4%.
  • Auto segment operating margins narrowed to 7.1% from 8.9% as the company absorbed 400–500 basis points of commodity inflation linked to the Middle East conflict.
  • Mahindra raised vehicle prices twice this year, including a July 8 hike, but said no further increases are immediately planned.

Strong Demand Drives Revenue Surge

Mahindra & Mahindra reported first-quarter revenue growth of 23% to ₹419.2 billion, powered by a 24.4% jump in its SUV segment to ₹310.33 billion. The results, announced Thursday, underscored the automaker's dominance in India's sport-utility market even as input costs surge.

The farm equipment segment — Mahindra's most profitable division — posted revenue growth of 19% to ₹109.47 billion, with volumes climbing 18% to 158,000 units. Government tax cuts introduced last September continued to underpin tractor demand across rural India.

"We're doubling EV production capacity, and that's going to be a key driver of growth over the next few years."

— Anish Shah, Managing Director and CEO, Mahindra & Mahindra

Commodity Inflation Hits Margins

The headline profit figure masked margin pressure in the auto business. Standalone operating margins in the segment narrowed to 7.1% from 8.9% a year earlier, a direct consequence of the Strait of Hormuz disruption that has sent aluminum, steel and petrochemical prices sharply higher since late February.

Group CFO Amarjyoti Barua said Mahindra absorbed between 400 and 500 basis points of commodity inflation during the quarter, managing costs through supply-chain execution rather than aggressive pass-throughs. The company implemented a second round of price hikes on July 8 but signaled no immediate plans for additional increases, leaving the decision contingent on commodity trajectories.

EV Expansion Takes Center Stage

Mahindra currently operates EV production capacity of roughly 96,000 units annually at its Chakan facility near Pune and plans to scale that to 144,000 units by March 2027. The company's born-electric portfolio — the XEV 9e, BE 6 and the recently launched XEV 9S three-row electric SUV — has gained steady traction, particularly in southern India.

Executive Director Rajesh Jejurikar has said the XEV 9S is expected to become Mahindra's best-selling EV and open new markets in North India, where larger SUV-style vehicles command strong demand. Six additional battery-electric models are planned through 2031 under Mahindra's revised "New Aspiration 2031" roadmap, which targets 16 new SUV launches — 10 internal-combustion and six electric.

A new greenfield plant in Nagpur, announced to support longer-term volumes, is expected to come online in 2028 and will produce the Vision X concept-based SUV alongside other next-generation models built on Mahindra's NU_IQ multi-energy platform.

The Indian EV Race Heats Up

Mahindra's capacity push comes as India's passenger-vehicle makers accelerate electric investments. Tata Motors, the current EV market leader, is expanding its own lineup, while Hyundai's Creta Electric and several Chinese-partnered brands are competing for share in a market where EV adoption is accelerating alongside tightening emission norms.

For Indian diaspora investors watching the auto sector, Mahindra's dual bet — rural tractor demand and urban EV growth — offers exposure to two structural themes in the Indian economy. The stock has outperformed the Nifty Auto index this year, though margin compression from the commodity cycle remains a near-term headwind.

What to Watch

Commodity cost trajectories through the second half will determine whether Mahindra needs further price increases. The September launch window for the NU_IQ platform's first production model and progress on the Nagpur plant will be key milestones for the company's EV ambitions.
